title: Cost optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Samuel Ortiz
release_notes:
Adds an autotune service that suggests and applies safe batching/caching defaults, ships quantization profile management, and includes unit-economics dashboards and CLI tooling. Backward compatible.
- Feature: Autotune defaults (batching/caching)
- Feature: Quantization profile registry + rollout support
- Tooling: Unit-economics dashboard + CLI report
- Ops: Metrics and alerts for regressions
description:
Motivation: Production customers repeatedly tune batching, KV caching TTLs, and quantization profiles manually. This leads to suboptimal unit economics and frequent ops toil. This PR: 1) introduces an autotune engine that recommends safe defaults for request batching and KV cache policies based on observed latency/throughput/seq-distribution; 2) adds a quantization-profile registry and rollout path so we can test lower-precision profiles with automated quality gating; 3) wires unit-economics tooling into Redwood Optimize and the Console so teams see per-route/token cost impact and estimated savings from suggested changes.

Design & Scope: The autotune engine collects per-model and per-route telemetry (p50/p95 latency, throughput, seq length histogram, model memory pressure) and runs a simple cost model to recommend a tuple {batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, cache_ttl_ms, quant_profile}. Recommendations are surfaced in the Optimize UI and can be applied automatically under a feature flag. Quantization profiles are YAML-defined artifacts stored in the model registry; each profile includes expected memory footprint, supported ops, and a quality delta estimate. The unit-econ tooling is a backend job that computes delta cost-per-inference and a 30-day savings forecast if the change is adopted.

Checklist:
- [x] Autotune engine (initial heuristic + safety caps)
- [x] Quant profile registry and onboarding APIs
- [x] Console UI card and CSV export for unit-econ reports
- [x] CLI: redwood optimize report --route <route> --recommendations
- [x] End-to-end tests (simulated traffic + perf regression checks)
- [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan

Commits summary: 
- feat(autotune): initial engine + heuristics (samuel/commit 1)
- feat(quant): add quant profiles schema + registry integration (samuel/commit 2)
- feat(uecon): unit-economic job and dashboard APIs (samuel/commit 3)
- fix(tests): stabilize perf test harness and mocks (samuel/commit 4)
- docs(optimize): docs and runbook for autotune (samuel/commit 5)

Files changed (high-level): optimize/autotuner.py, optimize/strategies.py, optimize/uecon/dashboard.py, optimize/uecon/job_runner.py, serving/batcher.py, serving/kv_cache.py, models/quant_profiles.yaml, model-registry/api.py, console/static/js/uecon-card.tsx, console/static/css/uecon.css, cli/commands/optimize_report.py, tests/test_autotune.py, tests/test_quant_profiles.py, docs/optimize/autotune.md, infra/k8s/helm/redwood-optimize-values.yaml, monitoring/alerts/optimize-alerts.yaml, scripts/regression/perf_check.sh, README.md. Changes are intentionally high-level; no large diffs in core runtime paths other than careful, opt-in hooks.

Testing & CI: CI run passed: build, unit tests (coverage net +0.3%), lint, e2e smoke, and perf-regression checks. The perf-regression harness runs a small load generator against a pinned model and validated that latency improved ~3% p95 in the median of test runs. We added a new perf job to CI that will guard against model-specific regressions on quant profiles.

Review conversation (high level):
- Aisha: "Can we add a safety cap on max batch size for latency-sensitive routes?" 
- Samuel: "Added a per-route override and a global safety cap; documented in docs/optimize/autotune.md."
- Marco: "How are we estimating quality delta for quant profiles?"
- Samuel: "We compute a small eval suite during profile onboarding and store a 90% confidence interval. The UI surfaces the confidence and requires manual approval when below threshold."
- Diana: "Make sure feature flag defaults to off for Dedicated/private customers."
- Samuel: "Defaulted the flag to off for private installs and added an opt-in toggle in the Console for Dedicated customers."

Rollout & Ops notes: Feature gated behind `optimize.autotune.enabled`. Staged rollout: enable in canary region for 2 weeks, validate UEcon dashboard and perf signals, then enable auto-apply for low-risk routes (low latency sensitivity). Metric alerts added: unexpected p95 increase > 10% post-apply, unit-econ delta negative > 5% (safeguard). We included rollback helpers in the console to revert applied recommendations.

Merge: squash merged to main after approvals from reviewers and green CI. Backwards compatibility: no change to public API surface; quant profiles are additive and gated.

Notes for operators: For on-prem installs, uplift the `redwood-optimize-values.yaml` and set `autotune.enabled=false` by default. There is a migration script (scripts/regression/perf_check.sh) used by CI but also available to SREs to validate local clusters.
